# Orch v0.1.1

This release closes the access and credential gaps found in a security review of the first release, lets a machine
a person connected offer what it can, and makes starting work follow the access people were given.

## Update

No manual database or configuration changes are needed. Download the release files for your architecture and run
`./update.sh v0.1.1 --from <directory with the release files>` in the deployment directory; `deploy/README.md`
describes updates and rollback. Unchanged Default and Developer tools templates switch to editable Dockerfile
templates at the first start; each host builds their image the first time an environment needs it.

## Security

- **Nobody gives more than they hold.** Invitations of every kind, member moves, org deletions, owner changes,
  approved access requests and lifted suspensions are judged by the same rule as a direct grant: the giver's own
  standing when giving, and again when a deferred grant takes effect. An API token gives no more than its scope, and a
  time-limited role keeps its end when its member moves.
- **Credentials end with their authority.** A tool connection ticket names the environment and generation it was
  issued for, and a resumed connection stays bound to the ticket that opened it; an agent reaches only the tool
  servers its session was given. Shell, agent terminal, browser and display viewer, and port access stay bound to the
  credential that opened them. A changed email address ends recovery links and codes sent to the old one; machine
  enrollment tokens are checked against their issuer; new API tokens respect the session's second step; sign-in
  cookies and identity-provider links are bound to the browser that started them.
- **Secrets stay secret.** Presented credentials are kept out of model error records and notification results,
  credentials pass through model gateways only to their provider, and skill archive imports cannot reach private
  network addresses.
- **What people see follows their access.** Search, outage notices, adopted threads, previews, document conversions
  and links in messages show nothing a reader may not read; unsafe message links stay inert.

## Machines a person connects

- A connected machine finds the Codex and Claude Code programs installed on it. A person who manages the machine
  confirms one before it is used; threads there then run that agent on the machine, with the provider owner's
  consent, and fall back to Orch's own tools otherwise.

## Starting work

- **Use of an environment starts threads.** Whoever may use an environment can start a thread in it; Manage is for
  setting the environment up and deciding who uses it.
- **Start threads and Create topics** can be given alone, on a topic and on a project. The middle level of an
  organization, project and topic is now called **Contribute** and includes both; Interact keeps its meaning for
  threads and chats, where it means talking to the agent and people.
- **The environment picker** lists what you can use first. Environments you can see but not use follow under
  **Ask for access**; picking one opens the access request for its Use.
- **The new-thread form** says whether the Directory you type exists in the environment or will be created.
- **Access requests** can ask for a chosen period; one that became unavailable can be asked again.

## Turns and approvals

- Inputs that have not started survive a lost session, Stop and a disabled resource; Stop is honoured while a turn
  is being prepared; queued starts recover after an interruption within their deadline; Retry says where the
  original message waits. A steer is checked against the running turn's model and the sender's current access.
  Approval and plan answers stay with their own turn and use the approver's authority, and unanswered requests are
  withdrawn when a turn stops. An unknown Codex outcome is reported as a failure.

## Environments and documents

- Default and Developer tools are editable Dockerfile templates, built on each host when first needed.
- A full disk while preparing an image is reported as a capacity problem; attached files and shells stay in the
  verified directory.
- The Local embeddings provider can be added.
- Restoring a document version refuses an incomplete one; undoing an import keeps concurrent edits and the recovery
  dates of what it removed; concurrent discussions and chat edits stay consistent.

## Installation and updates

- Installers report failures (BusyBox `wget`, PowerShell foreground runs), keep proxy settings in the node's service,
  name how to remove only the service, and install the x86-64 connector on Windows on ARM. Updates recover when
  interrupted before a backup, keep the port-signing key readable, and warn before rolling back to an incompatible
  connector minimum.

## Platforms and release

- Connectors and environment hosts are tested on Linux, macOS and Windows; Windows ends process trees by verified
  identity and recomputes file hashes it cannot verify.
- Release packaging fetches every crate it lists in the third-party notices and reuses dependency caches and
  verified native builds; CI runs the whole test suite in shards.
